**A Blues Scale in the key of A (A major)**  

| Scale degree | Note | Interval from the root |
|--------------|------|------------------------|
| 1 (root)     | **A** | 1 (unison) |
| b3 (minor 3rd) | **C** | minor third |
| 4 (perfect 4th) | **D** | perfect fourth |
| b5 (diminished 5th / “blue” note) | **D♯** | diminished fifth (♭5) |
| 5 (perfect 5th) | **E** | perfect fifth |
| b7 (minor 7th) | **G** | minor seventh |

**Pattern (intervals)**  
```
1 – b3 – 4 – b5 – 5 – b7
```

So the A blues scale is:

```
A – C – D – D♯ – E – G
```

This is the standard minor‑pentatonic (A, C, D, E, G) with the added “blue” note D♯ (the flattened fifth). It works over A‑major chords as well as A‑minor or any blues progression that centers on A.
